title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page lists several equivalent ways to define a projective structure on a smooth relative curve X/S. It works algebraically and characteristic-free in the relative setting, with ω = Ω^1_{X/S} and the principal-parts sheaves P^n_{X/S}. The previous page studied horizontal sections of P(P^1_{X/S}(ω)) and pulled back the canonical projective connection of P^1_S. The next page proves the equivalence between (a) and (e) over C, via a projective atlas viewed as a PGL(2)-torsor of local charts, plus GAGA.

(a) A triple (P, c, σ):
- P is a P^1-bundle on X;
- c is a connection on P relative to S (flat, since X/S has relative dimension 1);
- σ is a section that is nowhere horizontal ("partout non stationnaire").
In modern terms this is a PGL_2-oper, or Gunning's indigenous bundle: the transversality of σ to the horizontal foliation makes the connection's second fundamental form at σ an isomorphism T_X ≅ σ*T_{P/X}.

(a') An equivalent formal-geometric version: (P, σ) together with an isomorphism of augmented algebras φ : O_{(P̂,σ)} ≅ P^∞_{X/S}. Here O_{(P̂,σ)} is the formal completion of P along σ and P^∞_{X/S} is the formal neighbourhood of the diagonal. The condition is that the connection transported onto the completion (from the canonical stratification of P^∞) extends to all of P. So a projective structure becomes a global algebraisation of the infinitesimal neighbourhood of the diagonal by a P^1-bundle.

(b) A Lie-algebra form. Take an sl(2)-type Lie algebra bundle V that is "quasi-split", with a filtration Ω = L_1 ⊂ L ⊂ V, where L/Ω ≅ O_X and V/L ≅ Sym^2(L)⊗Ω^{-1} (in effect Ω^{-1}). Equip V with a Lie-algebra connection c : V → V⊗ω satisfying:
- Griffiths transversality c(Ω) ⊂ L⊗ω;
- non-degeneracy: the composite Ω → L⊗ω → (L/Ω)⊗ω = ω is an isomorphism.
Grothendieck notes it suffices to give c on L, as a map into Sym^2 L ⊗ Ω^{-1} ⊗ ω compatible with the bracket. This is exactly the oper condition in adjoint form (Beilinson–Drinfeld), with the principal-nilpotent condition expressed as the isomorphism Ω ≅ ω.

(b') The canonical model is V_X = Sym^2(P^1(ω)⊗ω^{-1})⊗ω^{-1} ≅ Sym^2(P^1(ω))⊗ω^{-3}. Since P^1(ω)⊗ω^{-1} is an extension of O by ω, the graded pieces of V_X are ω, O, ω^{-1}, and Ω ≅ ω. So a projective structure is a Lie-algebra connection on this fixed bundle (with the side remark about d^1 : ω → P^1(ω)).

(c) Let P_X = P(P^1_{X/S}(ω)) with its tautological section σ_X. There is a canonical isomorphism φ_2 : O_{P_X}/J^3 ≅ P^2_{X/S}. A projective structure is then an extension φ_3 : O/J^4 ≅ P^3_{X/S}. This is the jet-level shadow of (a'): the 2-jet is canonical, and the choice of 3-jet is the Schwarzian datum, so these extensions form a torsor under ω^{⊗2}.

(d) A third-order ODE (relative to X) on P^1_X = P^1_S ×_S X, invariant under PGL(2)_X. Equivalently, it is a PGL_2-invariant subset of the 3-jets of maps X → P^1_S that are local isomorphisms to order 3. This is the Schwarzian equation {f, z} = q.

(e) (next page) Over C: a sheaf of local analytic charts X^an → P^1(C) forming a torsor under the constant sheaf PGL(2,C).

The purpose is a dictionary of projective structures ("uniformisations") in a relative algebraic setting. It is presumably tied to the Gauss–Manin/Picard–Fuchs material of this dossier: second-order Picard–Fuchs equations and their projective connections.
errors: No substantive errors. The statement 'Sym^2(L)⊗Ω^{-1}' as the quotient V/L is shorthand: Sym^2 of the rank-2 bundle gives graded pieces Ω^2, Ω, O, and after twisting the top quotient is Ω^{-1}. This is consistent. Item (d) is incomplete as a sentence (the definition of 'invariant equation' as a subset of 3-jets is only sketched). In (a) flatness of c is automatic for relative dimension 1, so it is not stated.

ideas.what: Projective structure on X/S as a P^1-bundle with connection and nowhere-horizontal section
ideas.where_published: not in EGA/SGA as far as I know

ideas.what: Formal version: isomorphism of the completion along σ with P^∞_{X/S}, with the transported stratification globalising
ideas.modern_name: projective structure as global algebraisation of the formal neighbourhood of the diagonal (cf. Cartan connections / jet description of opers)
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore (Cartan geometry); not standardly phrased this way

ideas.what: Filtered sl(2) Lie algebra bundle with transversal, non-degenerate connection
ideas.modern_name: oper in adjoint (Lie algebra) form; Drinfeld–Sokolov condition

ideas.what: Canonical model V_X = Sym^2(P^1(ω))⊗ω^{-3} with graded pieces ω, O, ω^{-1}
ideas.modern_name: adjoint bundle of the jet bundle J^1(ω^{-1/2}) (oper bundle)

ideas.what: Projective structure as an extension of the canonical iso O/J^3 ≅ P^2 to O/J^4 ≅ P^3
ideas.modern_name: Schwarzian / projective connection as a 3-jet datum, torsor under ω^2
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (Schwarzian); Deligne LNM 163 for algebraic projective structures; Tyurin

missed.claim: Around 1972 Grothendieck wrote a characteristic-free, relative (over S) list of equivalent definitions of projective structures. It includes an adjoint sl_2 'oper' formulation with transversality and non-degeneracy conditions, about two decades before Beilinson–Drinfeld coined 'opers' and before Mochizuki's relative indigenous bundles.
missed.quote: Algèbre de Lie de type sl(2) quasi-scindée Ω⊂L⊂V ... munie de connexion c ... telle que la composée Ω→L⊗ω→ω soit un iso
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical priority for the oper formalism in the relative algebraic setting. Grothendieck's link to Gauss–Manin and the Cartier operation in this dossier connects naturally to dormant opers and p-curvature (Mochizuki, Joshi–Pauly, Wakabayashi).

missed.claim: The formulation (a') characterises a projective structure as an algebraisation of the formal neighbourhood of the diagonal P^∞_{X/S} by a P^1-bundle with section, compatible with the canonical stratification. This is a neat Cartan-geometry-via-principal-parts viewpoint rarely stated explicitly in the oper literature.
missed.quote: φ iso O_(P̂,σ) ≃ P^∞_{X/S} d'Alg. augm. tel que la connexion transportée ... se globalise à P
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It gives a clean definition of projective (and plausibly higher G-oper) structures in arbitrary characteristic and in families. In characteristic p it relates to divided-power jets and Frobenius-projective structures.

deep.surprise_reason: The content is essentially the theory of projective structures and PGL_2-opers, well known today (Gunning, Deligne, Beilinson–Drinfeld, Mochizuki). What is notable is the early, relative, characteristic-free formulation with the adjoint oper condition and the formal-neighbourhood/principal-parts description, apparently unpublished by Grothendieck.
transcription_corrections: 'V_V' in (b) is the sl(2)-type Lie algebra bundle (written 𝒱 with a subscript); 'type 𝔰𝔩(2)' is written roughly as 'sl(2)'.
'section parti.[?] et non stationnaire' should read 'section partout non stationnaire' (nowhere horizontal).

In (d) the end reads roughly 'aux jets d'ordre 3 de sections de [Γ?] X → P^1_S qui sont des iso locaux d'ordre 3'; the inserted text near 'sections' looks like 'des anneaux'/'des immersions' rather than Γ (uncertain).
